title: ThreadBridge: Priority Sampler — Customer Feedback Synthesis (Apr 2028)
summary: Compact synthesis of 120+ customer threads sampled by priority signals (time-since-ask, ARR impact, repeat frequency). Includes 7 high-leverage micro-features, 3 quick mitigations, and recommended owners + rough effort bands.
body:
Purpose and sampling: 
This note brings together a fast, pragmatic synthesis of customer feedback from Apr 1–Apr 10 2028. We applied a lightweight "priority sampler": weight = (revenue_tier * 0.5) + (repeat_count * 0.3) + (severity_score * 0.2) + recency_bonus. The dataset was ~320 tickets and slack threads; we sampled 120 threads that scored highest and manually reviewed them. Goal: identify immediate risk flags, micro patches, and medium-term product moves that reduce friction and prevent churn in the next 90 days.

High-level signal themes (top-down):
1) Observability gaps for model rollouts — customers (enterprise & mid-market) report insufficient per-route attribution for fallbacks and rollbacks. They want: token-level cost attribution by model variant during canaries, and an event stream that ties rollout decisions to errors and latency spikes. Quote: "We rolled a canary and lost 8 hours figuring out which sub-route tripped the fallback — needs better breadcrumbs."

2) Quality vs cost tuning presets — many customers are asking for opinionated presets that map workload archetypes (single-turn summarization, chat assistant, retrieval-augmented answer) to batching/quantization and model flavor recommendations. They want a one-click suggestion in Console and an API hint.

3) Private deployment onboarding friction — networking scripts and KMS integration docs are incomplete for some firewall/air-gapped customers. Several threads paused deals while waiting for infra runbooks or an on-site validation window.

4) Streaming SDK ergonomics — developer teams reported edge cases where mid-stream tool-calls plus partial KV-cache reuse produce duplicate tokens on reconnect. This is a reproducible client-side pattern in 3 customers.

5) Billing / quota surprises for embeddings-heavy workloads — customers triggered very high read/write token billing when using batch-embeddings over long corpora; they expect clearer pre-run estimates and a dry-run mode for the embeddings pipeline.

6) Fallback behavior semantics — teams want configurable semantic guarantees for fallback responses (e.g., predictable length, structured error envelope, or cached-stub output). There are multiple product requests to support "graceful degrade" presets.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "If the canary fails, tell me which model and which route so my incident runbook can trigger automatically."
- "Give us a safe-low-cost mode that keeps hallucination risk low for retrieval-heavy queries."
- "Private deploy docs: missing firewall egress table + sample iptables snippet cost us a week."

Top 7 high-leverage micro-features (fast wins, impact x effort):
1) Canary breadcrumb export (impact: high, effort: small) — export per-request model variant metadata and fallback chain to S3/LogEndpoint with a standardized schema. Minimal server-side change + Console toggle.
2) Console "Cost Presets" (impact: high, effort: small-medium) — UI presets (Conservative, Balanced, Performance) that wire up batching, KV-cache TTLs, and quantization hints. Also expose APIs to fetch preset JSON.
3) Embeddings dry-run estimator (impact: medium, effort: small) — a quick utility that samples corpus and returns estimated token count and projected cost for a batch job.
4) Streaming reconnect dedupe helper (impact: medium, effort: small) — SDK helper function + sample pattern to dedupe duplicate tokens on reconnect for tool-calling flows.
5) Private deploy quickstart script (impact: high for sales, effort: medium) — a hardened script (iptables, KMS mapping, sample systemd units) and a short verification checklist for partner on-site validation.
6) Fallback envelope spec + templates (impact: medium, effort: small) — define structured fallback responses (code, user_message, fallback_variant) and ship templates for common use-cases.
7) Per-route cost alert webhook (impact: medium, effort: small) — webhook for route/model cost anomalies exceeding threshold; includes summary and example sample trace.

Three immediate mitigations (hotpatches we can do in 1–2 sprints):
A) Incident runbooks for canary rollouts — publish a short runbook and add a Console link to the canary page. (Owner: SRE; effort: 2 dev-days + doc).
B) Temporary UI hint on embeddings page explaining batch-size vs cost tradeoffs and linking to a scheduler pattern (Owner: Product Docs; effort: 1 doc-day).
C) SDK pattern snippet for streaming dedupe posted in samples repo and referenced in streaming docs (Owner: DevX; effort: 2 dev-days).

Quantified risk and sample customers:
- 4 enterprise customers paused private deploys pending firewall scripts (risk: deal delay; estimated ARR at risk: ~$420k).
- 6 mid-market customers hit unexpected embedding bills leading to reduced ingest frequency (risk: increased churn propensity; estimated short-term MRR impact: ~$18k).

Open questions & friction points observed during triage: 
- Which Console page should host the Cost Presets UI? (Console infra dependency noted; PM decision required.)
- Do we lock fallback envelope schema to a stable v1? Need legal/security review for structured error fields if they include identifiers.
- How much of the private quickstart can be shipped as "supported but not managed" vs professional services?

Cross-references (tickets / proposals):
- JIRA-CS-1842 (customer A embedding billing spike) — linked logs attached.
- JIRA-PROD-4201 (canary observability gap) — includes early repro steps.
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/probes/pull/87 (streaming dedupe helper prototype).

Proposed prioritization (90-day horizon):
- Priority 1 (0–30 days): Canary breadcrumb export, Incident runbooks, Embeddings UI hint, SDK pattern snippet.
- Priority 2 (30–60 days): Console Cost Presets (alpha), Per-route cost webhook, Fallback envelope templates.
- Priority 3 (60–90 days): Private deploy quickstart full package, Console API to fetch presets, rollout analytics for model variants.

Suggested owners and rough effort (T-shirt sizing):
- Canary breadcrumb export: SRE + infra (Small — 3 dev-days).
- Console Cost Presets: Product-hosted-api + Console (Medium — 3–4 sprints for iterative alpha).
- Embeddings estimator: Optimize + DevX (Small — 1 sprint).
- Private quickstart: Solutions Eng + Private Deployments (Medium — 2 sprints + validation).

Communication plan:
- Publish a short "what we're shipping" note to customers impacted by the embedding and canary issues within 10 business days. Highlight the dry-run estimator and runbook link.
- Host a 30-min sync with top 6 impacted customers to demo the dedupe pattern and collect live feedback for Console presets.

Next steps (owner + due):
- AVA: draft customer-facing note + list of impacted accounts (due 2028-04-24).
- RAVI: prototype breadcrumb export schema and sample logs (due 2028-04-28).
- LENA: write embedding UI hint + sample screenshots (due 2028-04-22).
- JONAH: merge streaming dedupe PR and cut a release note (due 2028-04-26).

Appendix: brief synthetic repro for streaming dedupe issue:
1) Client opens stream, emits partial tokens, triggers a tool-call that reestablishes a connection.
2) Server returns tool output and replays cached tokens without idempotency marker.
3) Client receives duplicate token sequence on reconnect.
Workaround: client should include an incremental resume-offset token that the runtime acknowledges. The SDK helper implements this pattern.

Summary take: focus on low-effort observability + guidance (runbooks, small UI hints, SDK snippets) first. Those reduce near-term churn risk and unblock sales. Mid-term, invest in Console presets and private quickstart to turn friction into a growth lever.
